conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I’m Dr. Lee, one of the neuro-oncology team. You’re here today for your 19th cycle of high-dose methotrexate. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’m okay. A little tired lately, but otherwise fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you started rituximab two weeks ago. That’s part of the new alternating regimen. Any side effects from that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, not really. Just felt a bit flushed during the infusion, but it passed quickly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s common and usually mild. We’ll monitor you closely today. We’ll give the methotrexate around noon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Do I need any special prep?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’ll start IV fluids to protect your kidneys and give sodium bicarbonate to keep your urine alkaline. That helps clear the methotrexate faster.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And the leucovorin? When does that start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start leucovorin 24 hours after the methotrexate. It helps protect your healthy cells from the chemo.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll stay here until the level drops low enough?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll check your methotrexate level daily. Once it’s below 0.2, and you’re stable, you can go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The methotrexate infusion is complete. You did well. Any nausea or headache so far?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just a little queasy, nothing bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you some lorazepam or compazine if it gets worse. We’re avoiding Zofran because it gave you headaches before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, thank you. That’s better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs look stable. Liver enzymes are slightly up, but that’s expected. Your creatinine is low at 0.5, so kidneys are doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. What about the methotrexate level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s at 0.48. Still a bit high, so we’ll keep going with fluids and bicarbonate. Leucovorin started last night as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my aspirin—I usually take that daily. Should I restart?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We held it to help the methotrexate clear faster. You’re getting heparin shots for clot prevention. We’ll restart aspirin when you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. Thanks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Great news—your methotrexate level is now 0.14. That’s low enough for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief! So I can go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, once we go over your discharge instructions. You’ll need to take leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate every six hours for three more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Same doses as in the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes—40 mg leucovorin and 1300 mg sodium bicarbonate every six hours. It’s important to finish all the doses.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my regular meds—can I restart everything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. All your usual medications—citalopram, gabapentin, asthma inhalers, and aspirin—should be restarted today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. My foot pain has been acting up. Is that still something to worry about?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s still chronic and not fully explained, but we don’t think it’s related to the lymphoma. Keep using gabapentin and oxycodone as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I see someone about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, follow up with your primary doctor. Maybe a neurology or pain specialist can help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your liver enzymes are a bit higher than baseline—31 for ALT, 37 for AST—but that’s mild and expected with methotrexate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No need for concern?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at this level. We’ll watch it next cycle. Your hemoglobin is stable at 10.7, so no anemia issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my mood’s been okay. Citalopram is helping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad to hear that. You’ve been through a lot, but you’re managing well. Keep taking it daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And the next chemo is in a month?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same plan—alternating methotrexate and rituximab. The oncology clinic will call to schedule it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate all your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You did great this cycle. Take care, and call if you have any problems.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick final check before discharge. You’re alert, vitals are stable, and labs are good. Ready to go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, definitely. I’m feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Remember—leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate every six hours for three days. And follow up with your team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve got it written down. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you next month.
